title: Six Minutes, One Story: The Science Behind the Joy of Reading
title_zh: 六分钟，一个故事：阅读的快乐从何而来
intro_zh: 本文约 950 词，围绕“阅读为什么让人快乐”这一主题，结合心理学与神经科学的多项真实研究（如苏塞克斯大学的减压实验、基德与卡斯塔诺的共情研究），从平静身体、心流沉浸、共情训练、心灵度假、想象力锻炼和阅读仪式感等角度展开，语言难度贴近 CET-4，适合做限时阅读训练。

paragraphs.en: It is 10:20 p.m. on a crowded train, and a woman is smiling at a paperback. Her day was long: meetings, emails, a delayed bus. Yet here she is, laughing quietly at a scene that exists only on paper. What is she getting from those pages that the phone in her bag cannot give her? Scientists have spent years asking a similar question, and their answers are more interesting than you might expect. Reading for pleasure—not for exams, not for work, but for the simple wish to know what happens next—turns out to be one of the cheapest and most reliable forms of happiness available to us.
paragraphs.zh: 晚上 10 点 20 分，拥挤的列车上，一位女士对着一本平装书微笑。她的一天很漫长：会议、邮件、延误的公交。可此刻，她正安静地为一幕只存在于纸上的场景而发笑。那些书页给了她什么，是她包里的手机给不了的？多年来，科学家一直在追问类似的问题，而答案比你可能预想的更有意思。为快乐而读——不为考试，不为工作，只为单纯地想知道接下来发生了什么——原来是我们所能拥有的最便宜、也最可靠的幸福来源之一。

paragraphs.en: The first gift of reading is a calmer body. In 2009, researchers at the University of Sussex asked volunteers to try different ways of relaxing, and then measured their heart rates and muscle tension. Reading silently for just six minutes slowed the heart and eased the muscles more than any other activity: stress fell by 68 percent. Listening to music came next, at 61 percent; a cup of tea or coffee, 54 percent; a walk, 42 percent; and playing video games, only 21 percent. The researchers explained that a book gives the mind a clear scene to focus on, so the worries of the day lose their grip for a while. Six minutes—not six hours. That is roughly the time it takes to read two or three pages.
paragraphs.zh: 阅读带来的第一份礼物，是更平静的身体。2009 年，苏塞克斯大学的研究者让志愿者尝试不同的放松方式，然后测量他们的心率和肌肉紧张程度。仅仅安静阅读六分钟，就比其他任何活动都更能让心跳放慢、肌肉放松：压力下降了 68%。其次是听音乐，61%；一杯茶或咖啡，54%；散步，42%；而玩电子游戏只有 21%。研究者解释说，书给了大脑一个清晰的场景去专注，于是当天的烦恼暂时失去了抓手。六分钟——不是六小时。这大约就是读两三页书的时间。

paragraphs.en: Then there is the strange losing of time that every reader knows. You sit down after dinner 'just for a chapter,' and the next thing you notice is midnight. Psychologists call this state 'flow': the feeling of being so absorbed in an activity that the self, the clock, and the noise around you all seem to disappear. Reading invites flow because it offers a clear goal (find out what happens), constant feedback (each sentence moves the story forward), and a level of difficulty that the reader controls. A slow reader can take a month; a fast one can finish in an evening. Nobody is watching. Nobody is grading. The only rule is that you keep turning the pages.
paragraphs.zh: 然后是每个读者都熟悉的奇妙的时间消失感。你晚饭后坐下来“只看一章”，而当你再次注意到时间时，已经是午夜了。心理学家把这种状态称为“心流”：感觉自己如此沉浸于一项活动之中，以至于自我、时钟和周围的噪音似乎都消失了。阅读之所以容易产生心流，是因为它目标清晰（想知道接下来会发生什么），有持续的反馈（每个句子都推动故事前进），而且阅读难度由读者自己掌控。读得慢的人可以读上一个月；读得快的人一晚就能读完。没有人在看。没有人在打分。唯一的规则就是继续翻页。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps the most surprising finding is that stories do not merely entertain us; they train us. In a well-known 2013 study, psychologists David Comer Kidd and Emanuele Castano gave volunteers different kinds of texts. Those who read literary fiction—stories that demand you imagine other minds—scored higher on tests of empathy, the ability to sense what another person feels. Brain-imaging studies point the same way. When people follow a novel closely, the areas of the brain linked to movement and feeling light up as if the events were happening to them. A character climbs a ladder and your muscles quietly prepare; a character is embarrassed and you wince. For a few hours, you live inside a life that is not yours.
paragraphs.zh: 也许最令人惊讶的发现是，故事不只是让我们娱乐，它们还在训练我们。在 2013 年一项著名的研究中，心理学家大卫·科默·基德和埃马努埃莱·卡斯塔诺给志愿者读了不同类型的文本。那些阅读文学小说——那种要求你想象他人内心的故事——的人在共情测试中得分更高，而共情就是感受他人所感的能力。脑成像研究也指向同一方向。当人们专注地跟随一部小说时，他们大脑中与运动和感受相关的区域会活跃起来，就好像那些事情正发生在他们身上。人物爬梯子，你的肌肉会悄悄准备发力；人物感到尴尬，你会替他皱眉。有那么几个小时，你活在一种并不属于你的人生里。

paragraphs.en: That leads to the second promise of reading: escape. The word sometimes sounds weak, as if running away from reality were a kind of failure. But rest is not failure. A 2020 survey by the reading charity BookTrust found that nearly half of British adults said reading helped them cope with difficult emotions, and many said they read specifically to reduce worry. Think of it as a short trip that costs nothing. You cannot afford a flight to Iceland this weekend, but you can spend an afternoon in a village on its coast, learning how the light changes at midnight. The body stays in the armchair; the mind gets a holiday. When you return, the room looks the same, but your head is quieter.
paragraphs.zh: 这就引出了阅读的第二个承诺：逃避。这个词有时听起来有点弱，好像逃离现实是一种失败。但休息并不是失败。2020 年，阅读慈善机构 BookTrust 的一项调查发现，近一半的英国成年人说阅读帮助他们应对困难情绪，许多人说他们读书就是为了减少担忧。不妨把它看作一次不花分文的短途旅行。这个周末你负担不起飞往冰岛的机票，但你可以花一个下午待在一个海边村庄，看那里的光在午夜如何变幻。身体留在扶手椅里，心灵却去度了个假。当你回来时，房间还是老样子，但你的脑子安静多了。

paragraphs.en: Reading also gives us something that scrolling rarely does: a workout for the imagination. A film shows you a dragon; a book asks you to build one. In the 18th century, the writer and critic Samuel Johnson said that a reader's imagination is at work 'in a lazy calm,' quietly making pictures out of black marks on a page. That work is pleasant precisely because it is personal. Your version of a character's face will never match mine, and that is not a problem; it is the whole point. Even the physical act is gentle—slow breathing, steady eyes, no bright light pressing into the brain at midnight. In an age of endless feeds, this slowness feels less like a limitation and more like a gift.
paragraphs.zh: 阅读还给了我们一种刷手机很少能给的东西：对想象力的锻炼。电影直接给你一条龙；书却要求你自己把那条龙造出来。18 世纪，作家兼批评家塞缪尔·约翰逊说，读者的想象力是在一种“懒散的平静”中工作的，悄悄地把纸页上的黑色符号变成画面。这种工作之所以令人愉快，恰恰因为它是个人的。你想象中某个角色的脸永远不会和我的完全一样，而这不是问题；这正是关键所在。就连身体的动作也是轻柔的——缓慢的呼吸，平稳的目光，没有刺眼的强光在午夜直射大脑。在一个信息流无尽滚动的时代，这种缓慢显得不像是缺陷，而更像一份礼物。

paragraphs.en: Happiness grows more reliable when it has a routine. Many readers swear by the same small ceremony: a cup of tea, a lamp, twenty minutes before sleep. Doctors like it too, because replacing a phone screen with a printed page helps the brain slow down before rest. Reading is also social in a way that surprises people who picture readers as lonely. Book clubs turn a private pleasure into a monthly conversation; online communities such as BookTok have sent old novels back onto bestseller lists, with young readers recording tearful reactions to a single chapter. A story that moved you becomes more valuable when you can hand it to someone else and say, 'You have to read this.'
paragraphs.zh: 当快乐有了一种常规，它就会变得更可靠。许多读者都信守同一种小小的仪式：一杯茶，一盏灯，睡前二十分钟。医生也喜欢这样，因为用印刷页面替换手机屏幕有助于让大脑在休息前慢下来。阅读也具有社交性，这一点会让那些把读者想象成孤独者的人感到意外。读书会把这件私人的乐事变成每月一次的交谈；像 BookTok 这样的在线社区把旧小说重新送上畅销榜，年轻读者会录下自己读完某一章后泪流满面的反应。当你能把感动过你的故事递给别人，说一句“你一定得读读这个”时，它的价值就更高了。

paragraphs.en: None of this requires talent, money, or special equipment. A library card is free. A second-hand paperback costs less than two cups of coffee. What reading offers is not a dramatic high but an ordinary, repeatable joy: a slower heart, a quieter mind, a wider imagination, and the small shock of recognizing yourself in a stranger's story. The next time you feel restless, try six pages instead of six minutes of scrolling. You may find that the oldest form of entertainment is still one of the best.
paragraphs.zh: 这一切都不需要天赋、金钱或特殊设备。一张图书馆借书卡是免费的。一本二手平装书比两杯咖啡还便宜。阅读提供的不是戏剧性的高潮，而是一种普通而可重复的快乐：更慢的心跳，更安静的头脑，更广阔的想象力，以及在一个陌生人的故事里认出自己时那种小小的震动。下次你感到烦躁时，不妨试试读六页书，而不是刷六分钟手机。你可能会发现，最古老的娱乐方式仍然是最好的之一。

questions.q: According to the 2009 study at the University of Sussex, which activity reduced stress the most?
questions.explain: 原文第二段指出，安静阅读六分钟使压力下降 68%，高于听音乐（61%）、喝茶或咖啡（54%）、散步（42%）和玩电子游戏（21%），因此选 B。

questions.q: In Paragraph 3, the phrase 'so absorbed in an activity' is closest in meaning to:
options: worried about the result of an activity
questions.explain: absorbed 在此表示完全沉浸、全神贯注于某项活动，与 completely drawn into 意思最接近，故选 B。

questions.q: What does the writer mean by 'The body stays in the armchair; the mind gets a holiday'?
options: Reading offers rest without costing money or leaving home.
Readers should not stand up or move while reading.
Real travel is less valuable than reading a novel.
Readers often forget where they are sitting.
questions.explain: 该句强调阅读是一种低成本、足不出户的休息方式：身体留在原地，心灵却仿佛去度假，因此 A 最符合文意。

questions.q: Which of the following best summarizes the main idea of the passage?
options: Reading is better than video games because games make people nervous.
The joy of reading comes from calmness, absorption, empathy, imagination and daily rituals.
Only literary fiction can truly improve a person's ability to feel for others.
Reading is mainly a useful tool for students preparing for examinations.
questions.explain: 全文从减压、心流沉浸、共情训练、心灵度假、想象力和阅读习惯与社群等角度说明阅读为何让人快乐，B 概括最全面；A、C、D 均过于绝对或偏离主旨。
